extracted.intended_audience: ProofWiki contributors / editors (new and experienced users creating or editing pages)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and house-style rules for creating, naming, structuring, and formatting pages (definitions, theorems, proofs, and related sections) on ProofWiki.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating a page — methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Several ways to create a page: via search (click the 'Create the page "Proof name"' link), by following a red link, or by entering a direct URL and clicking 'create this page'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a page does not exist, use the search-created link, red links, or type the URL (e.g. http://www.proofwiki.org/wiki/Riemann Hypothesis) to open the edit window and start writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deleting a page
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't do this. Only trusted users can delete pages. If you feel a page needs to be deleted, add {{Delete}} to the top of the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unilateral deletions; use the Delete template to flag pages for deletion rather than removing content yourself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of choosing a good page title
rubrics_metrics.description: A good page title makes the page easier to search for, gives a first impression, adds to understanding, is used in links, and avoids name conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick descriptive, unambiguous titles so readers can guess content from the title and links convey meaningful information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific in page names
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no such thing as being too specific; single-word page names should generally be avoided because of ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/anti-patterns: not 'Definition:Prime Ideal' but 'Definition:Prime Ideal of Ring'; not 'Definition:Supremum' but 'Definition:Supremum of Subset of Real Numbers'. Include at least one noun, use 'of' where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid redundant words / articles in titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Page names should not be started with articles such as 'A' or 'The'; similarly, it's not necessary to begin the name with 'Proof of ...' since ProofWiki is a collection of proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Pythagorean Theorem' not 'The Pythagorean Theorem'. Exception: subtypes named like 'of the nth kind' (e.g. 'Elliptic Integral of the First Kind') may include such phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptiveness for theorems and equivalences
rubrics_metrics.description: A good page title describes the content accurately; for equivalence proofs, the title should make this clear by using 'iff'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since theorems are linked by exact page title, make theorem titles informative so a reader can guess the statement without visiting the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't blindly trust literature — prefer unambiguous names
rubrics_metrics.description: Books may use simplified terminology; ProofWiki cannot. Research for name conflicts and prefer more specific names; use the commonly used name only if there is no ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a theorem's conventional name is ambiguous or obscure, use a more descriptive title; when unambiguous, prefer the usual name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Namespaces for page types
rubrics_metrics.description: Use namespace prefixes for page types: prepend 'Definition:', 'Symbol:', 'Axiom:' etc. when appropriate and add the page to corresponding categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: name a definition page 'Definition:Calculus' and add it to Category:Definitions. See Help:Categories for details on categorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rules for page titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Page titles are case-sensitive; major words should be capitalized. Certain short words are not considered 'major' and ought to be lowercase (prepositions, pronouns, conjunctions, and short verbs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of lowercase words: and, as, by, for, from, if, iff, in, of, on, or, the, to, is, has, have, etc. Variables in formulas tend not to be capitalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names with formulas — formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If the page name contains mathematical statements: put no spaces between numbers that are added, subtracted, divided, or multiplied together; put spaces between elements related by equality/inequality; use '!=' for inequality. Variables need not be capitalized. No LaTeX commands in page names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: write '(1+2)x3' (no spaces between 1, +, 2) but '1 = 3/3 != 3/4' (spaces around '=' and '!='). Avoid LaTeX in titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of names named after mathematicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem or definition named after a mathematician gets a call of the {{Namedfor}} (or {{NamedforDef}}, {{NamedforAxiom}}) template; this places the page in the appropriate Named Theorems category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Namedfor template with the mathematician's name and category (surname). For multiple mathematicians, include multiple parameters as shown in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple names / aliases
rubrics_metrics.description: When a concept has several names, choose which one to use on ProofWiki (preference often for the mathematician's name unless obscure); create redirects or 'Also known as' sections as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create redirects for alternate names and use 'Also known as' sections to list alternative names (bold the names). Synthesize 'Also defined as' with 'Also known as' when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallowed characters in page names
rubrics_metrics.description: The following characters should not be used in page names: # < > [ ] | { } * & $ @
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using these characters; they are disallowed and will cause problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accented characters handling
rubrics_metrics.description: A theorem named after someone gets that exact name, including accented characters; for search convenience a redirect can be set up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact accented name for the main page and create redirects from unaccented variants via Help:Redirects#Accented characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: General page structure (default order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, pages follow this format: == Theorem == (state theorem), == Proof == (state proof), == Also see == (list internal links), == Sources == (citations), [[Category:The Category]].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this simple template for many pages; adapt as needed for definitions/other page types, but maintain the order and section headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required section order and capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections should be placed in this order with this exact capitalization (type 2 headings): Definition / Theorem, Proof(s), Also defined as, Examples, Also known as, Also see, Named for, Historical Note, Linguistic Note, Technical Note, Sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All of these should have a type 2 heading. Optional later sections include Lemma, Corollary, Outline of Proof, remarks, comments, notations, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and Theorems structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions/theorems are split into two parts: first a series of lines (typically starting with 'Let') introducing names and concepts needed, then separated by two blank lines the definition or theorem itself is stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display the concept being defined in bold (three apostrophes) throughout the page to make it stand out. Follow the 'Let ...' then blank-lines then statement pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides adhering to house style, separate different stages of the proof by subsections or whitespace; rigour is the only real prerequisite for proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you would like others to check your proof, add the {{Proofread}} template/call for proofreading. Use clear separation of proof stages to aid readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid general 'Notes' sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to avoid having a general 'Notes' section on a page; instead put remarks into one of the specified sections (Explanation, Technical Note, Linguistic Note, Historical Note, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This keeps pages structured and content placed where readers expect it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'Explanation' section
rubrics_metrics.description: This section can be used to explain concepts, particularly on definition pages or pages describing proof types; to give context, consider using an 'Also see' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put contextual explanation here rather than loose notes; link related material via 'Also see'.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Also defined as' section usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this section when a single name is used in the literature for multiple definitions (typically within the same field); if in other cases, prefer a disambiguation page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a synthesis with 'Also known as' where relevant and consult Help:Disambiguation for cross-field name conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Also known as' section usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this section when a concept or result is referred to in multiple ways, most commonly for definitions; all names should appear in bold and draw attention to possible name collisions with links/comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an alternative name coincides with another ProofWiki page, include a link and a clarifying comment. Bold all listed names.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Also see' section conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Also see' section should contain references to closely related concepts/results as a bulleted list; definitions should be referenced directly without providing a reader view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: '* [[Definition:Increasing Sequence of Sets]]' is correct. Also, when referencing a category, use the {{Link-to-category}} template and follow Template:Link-to-category documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of Name / Namedfor template usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Source of Name' section is exclusively created by the {{Namedfor}} template and is entered using parameters specifying the mathematician (and category for surname).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multiple mathematicians, use multiple parameters; this is analogous for definitions and axioms via NamedforDef and NamedforAxiom templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical Note guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Historical Note section is a relatively free-form area to elaborate on interesting information about the concept; short notes may be added after the Namedfor template instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a great deal to say, consider creating a transcluded page and/or a category for history material; use examples on the site as models (Fermat examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic Note guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a term is not common in natural language, indicate linguistic characteristics such as pronunciation, plural form, or etymology in this section; all words relating directly to the term should be bold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronunciation should be given in simple phonetic English with hyphenated syllables and stressed syllables in italics. Note UK/US spelling differences here when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Note guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: On definition pages, when rendering notation with LaTeX requires involved trickery, explain the code in a 'Technical Note' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Technical Note to document implementation/formatting details (example: Definition:Convergence in Measure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources section importance
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Sources' section serves to list the sources backing up a page; this section is of paramount importance for reliability and is discussed in detail on Help:Sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full citations in Sources and follow the guidance on Help:Sources to ensure verifiability and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories placement
rubrics_metrics.description: At the very bottom of the page, categories have to be added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Help:Categories for documentation on how to add categories properly; categories help indexing and navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional sections and miscellaneous
rubrics_metrics.description: Other optional sections include Lemma, Corollary, Outline of Proof, and more (remarks, comments, notations) for which there are no written guidelines yet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place optional sections sensibly after the main required sections; use the established heading style and ordering conventions.
